sentences.text: The case of the plaintiff is that defendant no. 1 is the builder and defendant no. 2 is the owner of the property bearing no. 21C, measuring area 50 sq. yds., situated in the layout plan of East Arjun Nagar, Lehari Colony, Delhi - 110032.
It is stated that both the defendants have approached the plaintiffs and showed them one collaboration agreement dated 27.09.2014 executed between the said defendants.

It is further stated that, as per said agreement, defendant no. 2 is the owner of the whole property and entire upper ground floor up to ceiling level without roof rights stand transferred to defendant no. 1,it was given as consideration in lieu of construction work done by defendant no. 1.
Thus, both the defendants have proposed the plaintiffs to buy the aforesaid property as they were in dire need of money for constructing the same.

3. It is further stated that thereafter, on 29.12.2014, the plaintiffs had entered into an agreement with the defendants for sale in respect of property bearing no. 21C, measuring area 50 sq. yds.,
Upper Ground Floor, upto the ceiling level, consisting of two room set, fitted with electricity and water tap with their meters, alongwith one scooter parking in stilt floor situated in the layout plan of East Arjun Nagar, Lehari Colony, Delhi - 110032 for a consideration amount of Rs.17,50,000/.
Thereafter on demand of the defendants, the plaintiffs have paid a sum of Rs.8 lakhs to the defendants as earnest money and balance money of Rs.9,50,000/ was Suit No.: 644/17 Krishna Kumar Yadav & Anr. v/s. Sameer Gupta and Anr.
to be paid till 10.10.2015 by the plaintiffs to the defendants at the time of execution of sale deed.

4. It is further stated that on 03.08.2015, the plaintiffs visited the abovesaid property to check the progress of work and they come to know from Sh. Shiv Kumar Aggarwal (defendant no. 2 herein)
that on 16.02.2015, the defendants had further entered into an agreement to sell with Smt.
Paramjeet Kaur with regard to the same property.
Thereafter, the plaintiffs had asked the defendants about the same, however, no satisfactory answer has been forthcoming from the defendants.
Upon this, the plaintiffs had asked for double amount of earnest money from the defendants to which they abused and used filthy language to the plaintiffs.
In this regard, an FIR bearing no. 1012/15 u/s. 420 IPC PS Farsh Bazar against defendant no. 1 has also been lodged by the plaintiffs and said defendant no. 1 was in JC.

However, prior to moving the bail application,
defendants have assured the plaintiffs to transfer the property in their favour but, despite several requests, the defendants did not transfer or executed the sale documents in favour of the plaintiffs.
The defendants have also threatened the plaintiffs.
5. Plaintiffs have also issued a legal notice dated 07.07.2017.
Same has also been served upon the defendants but to no avail.

Thus, the present suit was filed by the plaintiffs for specific performance,
in alternative for recovery of Rs.8 lakhs.
He has also prayed for permanent injunction.
6. It may be noted that despite opportunities, defendant no. 1 had failed to file his written statement and his right to file WS was closed on 27.02.2018.
Thereafter, defendant no. 1 had not appeared and he was proceeded ex parte on 19.04.2018.

sentences.text: It is submitted that he only wishes to pursue this case for alternative relief of recovery of amount of Rs.8 lakhs.
15.Now, only issue no. 1, 2 and 4 remains to be decided.

Issue no. 1 :
Whether the suit of the plaintiff is bad for mis joinder parties?
OPD 16.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the defendant.
The defendant no. 2 has taken an objection that suit of the plaintiffs is bad for misjoinder of parties.

It is submitted that there is no privity of contract between the plaintiffs and defendant no.
2 and he has been unnecessary party in this case.
No evidence has been led on behalf of the defendant in this case.
However, the plaintiffs had examined 02 witnesses i.e. themselves as Krishan Kumar Yadav as PW1 and Sh. Inderjeet as PW2.
During the crossexamination of both the witnesses, it was admitted that there was no written agreement executed between the plaintiffs and defendant no. 2.

It was also stated that no amount was paid by the plaintiffs to defendant no.
2.
In that case, there is no agreement between the plaintiffs and defendant no. 2 and no amount has been paid to defendant no. 2.
Thus, there is no privity of contract between the parties.

Moreover, the Suit No.: 644/17 Krishna Kumar Yadav & ... vs . Sameer Gupta And Anr. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82249894/

sentences.text: Whether the suit is not properly valued for purpose of court fees and jurisdiction?
OPD 17.Objection was taken by the defendant that suit has not been properly valued for the purpose of court fees and jurisdiction.
No evidence has been led by the defendant on this aspect.
However, the plaintiffs in his valuation clause, has valued the suit for the purpose of court fees and jurisdiction at Rs.8 lakhs.
In view of the statement given by the plaintiffs on 09.08.2023, they have confined their suit only for the purpose of recovery of amount of Rs.8 lakhs.
On the recovery of the said amount of Rs. 8 lakhs necessary court fees of Rs.10,350/ has been paid.
Hence, the plaintiffs have properly valued the suit for the purpose of court fees and jurisdiction.
Thus, this issue is decided in favour of the plaintiffs.

Issue no. 4 :
Whether the plaintiff is alternative relief of recovery of Rs.8 lacs as claimed?
OPP 18.The onus to prove this issue was upon the plaintiffs.
The plaintiffs have stated that an agreement to sell was executed between the plaintiffs and defendant no. 1 and in pursuance of the agreement, they have paid an amount of Rs.8 lakhs.
The terms of the agreement were not complied with by the defendant no. 1 and they are entitled to the recovery of amount of Rs.8 lakhs paid by them.
19.The plaintiff no. 1 examined himself as PW1.

During his examination in chief, he sought to rely upon the documents i.e. agreement to sell, Suit No.: 644/17 Krishna Kumar Yadav & Anr. v/s. Sameer Gupta and Anr.
collaboration agreement and bank passbook.

Statement of account of plaintiff's bank account showing the amount transferred by the plaintiffs to defendant no. 1 was marked as Mark C.
The plaintiff no. 2 did not tender the original documents in his evidence and only relied upon the photocopies of documents produced by the plaintiff no. 1 in his evidence.

sentences.text: 5 20.The
plaintiffs have claimed that they have paid amount of Rs.8 lakhs which is reflected in agreement to sell.
However, the plaintiffs have not produced the original agreement on record.
They have also not filed on record their statement of account showing the amount paid by them to defendant no. 1 through cheques.

These were essential documents which have been withheld by the plaintiffs and they have chosen not to produce the original documents on record despite they being not exhibited during evidence as being photocopy.
The plaintiffs have also not sought permission from the court to rely upon secondary evidence.

As the amount was paid by the plaintiffs to defendant in pursuance of the agreement to sell, it was essential to produce the original documents i.e. agreement to sell and statement of accounts on record.

Only then, the contents of these documents would have proved that amount of Rs.8 lakhs was given by the plaintiffs to defendant no.
1.
There is only self serving statement of the plaintiffs to prove payment of Rs.8 lakhs made to defendant no. 1 and same is not enough to prove the case of the plaintiffs.
Suit No.: 644/17 Krishna Kumar Yadav & Anr. v/s. Sameer Gupta and Anr.

Hence, this issue is decided against the plaintiffs.

22.No order as to costs.
